ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure is a physical diagram of a slide. The length of the inclined section of the slide is $L=5.0\mathrm{m}$, and the height is $h{=}3.0$ m. To ensure the safety of children, a safety mat is laid on the horizontal surface. The horizontal section is smoothly connected to the inclined section, and the speed of the child remains unchanged at the connection point. A child starts sliding from the top of the slide from rest, passes the bottom of the inclined section, and then slides a certain distance horizontally before coming to a stop on the safety mat. The mass of the child is $m{=}20\mathrm{kg}$, the average resistance force on the inclined section is $f_{1}\mathrm{=}88\mathrm{N}$, and the average resistance force on the horizontal section is $f_{2}=100\mathrm{N}$. Air resistance is negligible, and the gravitational acceleration is taken as $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The work done by the child to overcome friction while sliding down the inclined plane.
2. The speed $v$ of the child when sliding to the bottom of the inclined plane
3. To prevent the child from sliding off the horizontal mat, the length $x$ of the mat must be at least how long?

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: it shows a child slide with a sloped section descending to a smoothly connected horizontal run-out/mat. Then use the text values L=5.0 m, h=3.0 m, m=20 kg, f1=88 N, f2=100 N, g=10 m/s^2. Compute friction-overcoming work on the incline as W_f1=f1 L. For the bottom speed, apply the work-energy theorem from rest: gravitational potential energy lost mgh minus work against incline resistance f1 L becomes kinetic energy, so (1/2)mv^2=mgh-f1L. For the mat length, use the kinetic energy at the bottom and set it equal to the horizontal friction work needed to stop: f2 x=(1/2)mv^2. This yields 440 J, 4 m/s, and 1.6 m.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: the slide consists of a straight inclined section followed by a horizontal safety mat, so motion can be split into an inclined-motion stage and a horizontal deceleration stage. Use the text values L=5.0 m and h=3.0 m to get sinθ=h/L=3/5 for the incline. The work to overcome incline friction is still f1L. For the bottom speed, apply Newton's second law along the incline: the downslope component of weight is mg sinθ, resistance f1 acts upslope, so a1=(mg sinθ-f1)/m. Starting from rest over distance L, use v^2=2a1L. For the horizontal mat, the only average retarding force is f2, giving a2=f2/m opposite the motion, and the stopping distance follows from 0=v^2-2a2x, so x=v^2/(2a2). 再推理：已知斜面长度 L=5.0 m，高度 h=3.0 m，所以 sinθ=h/L=3/5。1. 斜面上克服摩擦做功为 W=f1L=88×5.0=440 J。2. 沿斜面方向，重力分力为 mg sinθ=20×10×3/5=120 N，阻力 f1=88 N，合力为 120-88=32 N，所以加速度 a1=32/20=1.6 m/s^2。孩子从静止开始滑过 L=5.0 m，有 v^2=2a1L=2×1.6×5.0=16，所以 v=4 m/s。3. 水平段上阻力 f2=100 N，减速度大小 a2=f2/m=100/20=5 m/s^2。停止距离满足 0=v^2-2a2x，所以 x=v^2/(2a2)=16/(2×5)=1.6 m。

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure is a physical diagram of a slide. The length of the inclined section of the slide is $L=5.0\mathrm{m}$, and the height is $h=3.0\mathrm{m}$. To ensure the safety of children, a safety mat is laid on the horizontal surface. The horizontal section is smoothly connected to the inclined section, and the speed of the child remains unchanged at the connection point. A child starts sliding from the top of the slide from rest, passes the bottom of the inclined section, and then slides a certain distance horizontally before coming to a stop on the safety mat. The mass of the child is $m=20\mathrm{kg}$, the average resistance force on the inclined section is $f_1=88\mathrm{N}$, and the average resistance force on the horizontal section is $f_2=100\mathrm{N}$. Air resistance is negligible, and the gravitational acceleration is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m/s^2}$. 1. The work done by the child to overcome friction while sliding down the inclined plane. 2. The speed $v$ of the child when sliding to the bottom of the inclined plane. 3. To prevent the child from sliding off the horizontal mat, the length $x$ of the mat must be at least how long?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, a children's slide can be seen; the inclined slide extends downward from a higher platform, and after reaching the bottom it smoothly transitions to a nearly horizontal ground area, matching the structure in the problem statement in which the inclined section is connected to the horizontal safety mat. Reasoning: It is known that L=5.0 m, h=3.0 m, m=20 kg, f1=88 N, f2=100 N, g=10 m/s^2. 1. The work done to overcome friction on the inclined plane is W_f1=f1L=88×5.0=440 J. 2. Sliding from rest at the top to the bottom, the gravitational potential energy decreases by mgh=20×10×3.0=600 J, of which 440 J is used to overcome the resistance on the inclined plane, and the remainder is kinetic energy, so (1/2)mv^2=600-440=160 J. Substituting m=20 kg gives 10v^2=160, v^2=16, v=4 m/s. 3. After reaching the horizontal mat, it stops by relying on the horizontal resistance f2, requiring f2x=160 J, so x=160/100=1.6 m.
